opportunities.title: It Wasn't a Zero-Day. It Was a Laptop.: Binance's $6.3B Hack Is an HR Problem Wearing a Hoodie
opportunities.why_now: Blockaid's CEO now says the breach may trace to private key misuse via a single compromised engineer laptop, not a protocol exploit — the most damning root-cause claim yet.
opportunities.angle: Security postmortem breaking down why 'sophisticated attack' headlines keep losing to 'someone phished an employee,' with a checklist of what institutional custody should have caught

opportunities.title: $1.8B Frozen, $1.4B Untouchable: The Binance Hack Just Ran the Ultimate Stablecoin vs. Bitcoin Experiment
opportunities.why_now: Tether and Circle froze $1.8B in stolen funds within hours while the hacker split $1.4B in BTC into 19 wallets no one can touch — a live A/B test of 'programmable money' vs. 'sound money' happening in real time.
opportunities.angle: Markets/security crossover piece on what this split outcome means for institutional risk models and why BTC's unfreezability is a feature until it's the attacker's feature

opportunities.title: Your Hardware Wallet Was Compromised Before You Opened the Box
opportunities.why_now: Trezor just flagged a suspected hardware implant in Safe 5 units sold through third-party reseller CryptoBilis, meaning the attack vector was the supply chain, not the firmware.
opportunities.angle: Explainer on gray-market reseller risk with a concrete buying checklist (seal checks, direct-from-manufacturer purchasing, verification tools) — the piece people share before buying their next cold wallet

opportunities.title: EIP-7702 Didn't Cause the Binance Hack — It Just Made the Bleeding Faster
opportunities.why_now: Cointelegraph's new analysis says account abstraction via EIP-7702 amplified attacker throughput once the initial compromise occurred, a technical detail getting buried under hack headlines.
opportunities.angle: Deep-dive for the technically literate reader: how 7702 batch execution turns one stolen key into an irreversible drain in seconds, and what wallets/exchanges need to rate-limit now

opportunities.title: Institutions Are Pulling Funds Off Exchanges Right Now — Exactly the Trade 'Already Priced' Readers Made Years Ago
opportunities.why_now: CoinDesk reports institutional investors rushing to withdraw from exchanges post-hack, validating the self-custody thesis this channel has been pushing all along.
opportunities.angle: Vindication/I-told-you-so op-ed tying the outflow data to a practical self-custody framework, framed as 'what the smart money just relearned the hard way'
